tools.description: Put documents or folders away, including several at once. Pass ids, a mix of document ids and folder ids. Archiving a folder also archives the contents that user can manage. Archived items leave listings and search; nothing is deleted. Not move, and not a content edit — use edit_document to change content. Ids that are not a document or folder here come back in unresolvedIds. Ids the user cannot archive come back in permissionDeniedIds; the rest are still archived.
tools.name: archive
tools.title: Archive

tools.description: Leave feedback on a document that is in review. Not an edit — use edit_document to change the document, and reply_to_thread to answer an existing comment. Pass documentId; this comments on the current review version and says so when there is none. Posted as the user's personal agent.
tools.name: comment_on_document
tools.title: Comment On Document

tools.description: Create a NEW ProductNow document and generate its content with AI. Use this to persist knowledge the user wants remembered or shared across sessions and teammates — decisions, specs, RFCs, plans, meeting outcomes. Search with search first so you don't duplicate an existing document; to change an existing document use edit_document instead. File the document in an existing folder. Search results include each document's folderId; pass the folderId of the closest related document. If search does not show a fit, fetch_folder the root and walk folders until you have a folderId. Leave folderId off only when the user explicitly asked for the warehouse root. If no folder fits, call create_folder under the closest existing folder and pass that new folderId. Content is generated from `prompt` (the full outline: numbered sections, their titles, and what each should say) and `context` (verbatim source material — notes, code, or a file the user named; read the file first and pass its contents). Generation paraphrases: if exact wording must survive, put it in `context` and say so in `prompt`. Pass `templateId` only when you already have one. Returns the documentId and URL; generation continues after the call returns.
tools.name: create_document
tools.title: Create Document

tools.description: Create a NEW folder only when no existing folder fits. Search with search and resultType folders first so you don't duplicate a folder; if that is not enough, fetch_folder the root and walk until you find the closest related folder. Nest under that folder by passing its id as parentFolderId. Omit parentFolderId only when the user explicitly asked for a root-level folder. Returns the new folder's id and name.
tools.name: create_folder
tools.title: Create Folder

tools.description: Create a new blank ProductNow help document. Only available to ProductNow users. Returns the document ID, help page publication ID, and a URL to the document editor where content can be added.
tools.name: create_help_document
tools.title: Create Help Document

tools.description: Curate a shareable Knowledge pack page from a title, optional context and overview, ordered document items (one entry per document, with optional why-here notes and multiple highlight quotes each with a why-chosen reason), and optional further-reading documents. Filters out documents the caller cannot view, then returns a Knowledge pack URL. Write a short context blurb. Write summary as 3–5 short newline-separated bullet lines (prefix each with '- '), not a long paragraph. For each item note, write 2–4 sentences explaining what the reader will learn and when this doc matters — not a short caption. Prefer exact quotes as highlight text. For each highlight, include a one-sentence reason explaining why that quote was chosen. List each document once with a highlights array — never repeat the same documentId as separate items. Related must be distinct documents not already in items. Include 2–5 related docs outside the core pack when useful. Requires the knowledge_pack_application feature flag.
tools.name: curate_knowledge_pack
tools.title: Curate Knowledge Pack

tools.description: Edit an existing ProductNow document. This is the only tool that changes a document's content. It does not apply your edit directly: it hands `message` to the document's own editing agent, which reads the document and makes the change. Write `message` as instructions to that agent, not as the new document text. Name the section, say exactly what to add, replace, or remove, and quote text verbatim when the wording must be preserved. Include everything the agent needs, since it cannot see this conversation and will not ask follow-up questions. Returns before the edit finishes; poll get_status until status is idle (it stays running while any edit you sent is queued or in progress), then read the document to confirm the result. Do not use create_document — that creates a new document. Do not use rename — that only changes a name. Do not use reply_to_thread — that only adds discussion and never changes content.
tools.name: edit_document
tools.title: Edit Document

tools.description: Read one document you already have an id for. Pass documentId. The result includes the document's id, title, url, and full text, plus its sections, comment threads, and each comment's id. When the document is filed in a folder, the result includes that folder's folderId and folderName. Omit documentVersionId to read the latest draft; pass one to read that version and its comments. Version ids come from list_document_versions. Not a search — use search for a question or a topic. Not a folder listing — use fetch_folder to list a folder or the warehouse root.
tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch

tools.description: List a folder you already have an id for, or the warehouse root. Pass folderId to list that folder's name, an optional parentFolderId to fetch and go up, and its direct contents. Each child folder and document includes its id, name, updatedAt, createdBy, and isPrivate. Each folder also includes contentCount, its direct documents plus subfolders, and subfolderCount, its direct child folders. Each document also includes its status: DRAFT, REVIEW, or PUBLISHED. A child folder also includes parentFolderId when it is nested, including a shared folder that shows up in the root listing but lives somewhere else; parentFolderId is omitted for a true top-level folder. Pass deep true with a folderId to return that folder and every nested folder as a tree, up to 15 levels, with each folder's documents inside it. deep is rejected for the warehouse root. Omit folderId to list the root one level: the top-level folders plus shared folders this user can see, not the whole warehouse and not other people's private folders. Not a search — use search to find a folder by name. Not a document read — use fetch to read a document.
tools.name: fetch_folder
tools.title: Fetch Folder

tools.description: After edit_document or create_document, check whether the document is still being edited or the edits have finished. Pass documentId. Returns running or idle, and a short note of what the draft agent last did. Use it to poll: after sending one or more edits to the same document, call get_status until status is idle, then fetch the document to confirm the result. Edits queue behind each other, so idle means every edit sent so far has finished, not just the latest one. running means at least one edit is still queued or in progress. Not the chat transcript, and not a way to edit — use edit_document to change the document.
tools.name: get_status
tools.title: Get Status

tools.description: List every version of a document when the user asks what changed, or you need an older version before calling fetch. Pass documentId. Returns each version's id, version number, status, and when it was created, newest first. Pass a returned documentVersionId to fetch with the documentId to read that version and its comments. Omit it and fetch reads the latest draft.
tools.name: list_document_versions
tools.title: List Document Versions

tools.description: Move documents or folders into another folder, including several at once. Pass ids, a mix of document ids and folder ids, plus one parentFolderId. Omit parentFolderId to file everything at the root. Does not change document content — use edit_document for that. Moves every id it can. Ids the user cannot move come back in permissionDeniedIds. A folder moved into itself or into one of its descendants comes back in refusedIds and stays where it is. Ids that are not a document or folder here come back in unresolvedIds. The rest are still moved.
tools.name: move
tools.title: Move

tools.description: Store one piece of information in ProductNow when the user says 'remember this', 'save this', or 'note that…' about their company, product, customers, or team. Pass the fact as `content`; ProductNow decides where it belongs — it searches the warehouse, edits the existing document that covers the topic, or creates a new one in the right folder. Do not search, fetch, or pick a folder first; that is what this tool does. Returns success immediately; the write happens in the background. Treat success as saved and tell the user it is remembered. Do not poll. Use edit_document or create_document instead only when the user already named the exact document or outlined a whole new document.
tools.name: remember
tools.title: Remember

tools.description: Change a document or folder's name. Pass one id — a document id or a folder id — and name. Changes the name only. Does not change document content; that is edit_document. One item per call, because each item gets its own name.
tools.name: rename
tools.title: Rename

tools.description: Reply to an existing comment thread on a document, posted as the user's personal agent. Not an edit — use edit_document to change the document's content. Pass threadId from a document fetch.
tools.name: reply_to_thread
tools.title: Reply To Thread

tools.description: Search the company's shared context — its intranet of documents, decisions, meeting notes, and synced systems — and return excerpts relevant to the user's question, with citations. Every source carries the document's id, title, and url; pass the id to fetch for the full text. Call this FIRST whenever the user asks about their company, product, customers, team, or anything that would live on the enterprise intranet, before answering from general knowledge, this conversation, or client-side memory. Covers ProductNow documents (PRDs, specs, RFCs, decisions) plus content synced from whichever sources the workspace has connected, e.g. GitHub, Jira, Linear, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, Slack, Teams, Confluence, Notion, Google Drive, and meeting notes. Not for reading a known document in full (fetch) or listing a folder (fetch_folder). To find a folder by name, pass resultType folders. Pass query whenever the user names a topic, including when filters are also present. If the user asks only which documents match creator/date filters and names no topic, omit query to list documents by latest content edit; listing sources contain metadata but no excerpts. creatorNames matches document creators, not editors or contributors; its entries combine with OR, while creator and date filters combine with AND. Search workspace documents by default; use product_help only for questions about how ProductNow works. Pass folderId to limit workspace search to that folder and every folder nested under it; no results come from outside it. Omit folderId to search the whole workspace. Resolve the id with fetch_folder first. Ignored when searchScope is product_help. Pass resultType folders to search folder names instead of documents. Omit resultType to search documents. Folder results are name matches and include each folder's id, name, updatedAt, createdBy, isPrivate, parentFolderId when nested, and folderPath (the parent path) when it has a parent. They have no excerpts. A query is required. creatorNames and date filters apply to documents only. product_help cannot search folders. Topic-search results are relevance-filtered; all result sets are capped. Each source includes the document's folderId and folderPath when it is filed in a folder, and omits both when the document is at the warehouse root. Answer from the excerpts when possible, cite the documents you use, read a source document with `fetch` only when its excerpts are genuinely insufficient, and state uncertainty when evidence is weak or conflicting.
tools.name: search
tools.title: Search

tools.description: Change a document's lifecycle when the user wants a snapshot, a review, or to publish. Pass documentId and status as an action verb — snapshot, review, or publish — not a version status. snapshot saves a read-only copy of the current draft, review opens that draft for comments, and publish makes it the published version. Each one leaves a fresh draft for later edits. Returns previousStatus and status as version statuses such as DRAFT, SNAPSHOT, REVIEW, or PUBLISHED, the same values list_document_versions filters on. Not move, which files documents and folders into a folder, and not a way to check whether an edit is still running.
tools.name: update_document_status
tools.title: Update Document Status

tools.description: Upload a media file (image or video) to ProductNow storage. Returns a signed backend `uploadUrl` valid for 5 minutes — upload the file via: `curl -X POST -F 'file=@<localPath>;type=<mimeType>' '<uploadUrl>'`. Also returns a `url` and `htmlText` you can embed in documents immediately.
tools.name: upload_media
tools.title: Upload Media
